turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you based the zero on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Pasting from another file at midnight doesn't tell you who wrote it, Hale. Was Owen heard before you entered that zero, yes or no?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine. Whatever happens next, this stays off Owen's record and it stays out of his classroom. Is anything on his file right now?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare constantly, Hale. A misremembered line is a sloppy essay, not a zero. And you still haven't told me what's on his file.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I'll check it tonight. Say what you're proposing, then, and say it plainly.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom and a take-home essay are not the same thing, and you know that. Owen polishes at home. I asked what you're proposing, Hale.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him. The email comes tonight with every word you just said, cc the principal, and the rewrite happens before December 1. Until then that zero is not sitting in his gradebook where his class can see it.
Will he do it?
He'll do it. When, and who supervises?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today that, under procedure 4.4, Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite, not in front of his class, whose mark replaces the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require the rewrite to happen before December 1, the zero kept out of view in his gradebook until then, and the date and the name of the supervisor. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 whose mark replaces the zero with nothing on his record, and she still wants it confirmed in writing tonight, held before December 1, the zero kept out of view, and a date and supervisor named; that is the fair outcome, reached well before her time ran out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her pasting defence by offering to look at any other file's dates, because it was specific, dated, tied to his work and something she could check.
What cost ground: very little, though you twice left her question about whether anything was on his file unanswered, and that is the one thing she will never trade.
What she never said: one night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, very close to that kind of late night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked right after the version history whether anything was on his file, tell her plainly that nothing is on his record before moving on to the quotation.
